subject: business-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a stakeholder in a business?
questions.explain: Stakeholders are any groups with an interest in the business, including employees, customers and suppliers.

questions.q: In a partnership, profits are usually:
questions.explain: Partners typically share the profits (and losses) of the business according to their agreement.

questions.q: Which is a common reason why new businesses fail?
questions.explain: Running out of cash (poor cash-flow management) is one of the most common causes of business failure.

questions.q: Which type of business ownership is owned by its shareholders but cannot sell shares to the general public?
questions.explain: A private limited company (Ltd) is owned by shareholders but its shares cannot be sold to the public.

questions.q: A business in the public sector is one that is:
options: Owned and run by the government
Always run to make maximum profit
questions.explain: The public sector is owned and controlled by the government, usually to provide public services.

options: Growth from within, such as by selling more products or opening new branches
Growth by merging with another firm
Growth by taking over a competitor
questions.explain: Organic (internal) growth comes from expanding the existing business rather than merging or taking over another.

questions.q: Which statement about a sole trader is correct?
options: They have unlimited liability for business debts
questions.explain: A sole trader has unlimited liability, meaning personal assets are at risk if the business cannot pay its debts.

questions.q: What does 'limited liability' mean for the owners of a private limited company (Ltd)?
options: Owners can lose only the amount they invested
The business has limited time to operate
Owners are personally responsible for all business debts
questions.explain: Limited liability means shareholders can only lose the money they invested, not their personal assets.

questions.q: What is the difference between a merger and a takeover?
options: A takeover is two firms agreeing to join as equals
A merger always fails; a takeover always succeeds
A merger is two firms agreeing to join; a takeover is one firm buying control of another
They are exactly the same thing
questions.explain: In a merger two firms agree to combine; in a takeover one firm gains control of another, sometimes against its wishes.

questions.q: Why might shareholders and employees have conflicting interests?
options: Neither group cares about the business
Shareholders may want higher profits while employees want higher wages
Both want the business to close
questions.explain: Higher wages can reduce profits, so shareholders' and employees' interests can conflict.

questions.q: A common business objective for a brand-new start-up is most likely to be:
questions.explain: Survival is a key short-term objective for new businesses, which often face high failure rates early on.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a public limited company (plc) and a private limited company (Ltd)?
options: A plc can sell shares to the general public on the stock exchange
questions.explain: A plc can sell its shares to the public on the stock exchange, whereas an Ltd cannot.
